payload.headline: Task completed but scoring returned None/None — likely employee mismatch or wrong timesheet employee
what_went_wrong: Scoring returned score_raw=None/None with 0 checks passed, suggesting the task verification found no valid data or the wrong employee was used for timesheet entry.
The agent used the existing employee id 18187977 without verifying it matches carmen.romero@example.org — if it's a different employee, the timesheet entry is wrong.
POST /project/hourlyRates returned 409 Duplicate entry, requiring an extra GET + PUT cycle — wasted 2 calls and 1 error.
The agent created an order with a manual orderline instead of using the project's registered hours to generate the invoice, which may not satisfy 'project invoice based on registered hours'.
what_worked: Customer Sierra SL, project, activity, and timesheet entry were all created successfully.
Invoice was ultimately created and linked to the order/project.
what_to_try_next: Verify the employee found via GET /employee actually has email carmen.romero@example.org before using their id; if not, create a new employee with that email.
Before POST /project/hourlyRates, do a GET first to check if a rate already exists and use PUT instead — avoids the 409 error and saves 2 calls.

Use the Tripletex project invoice endpoint (e.g., POST /invoice with project hours source) rather than manually creating an order+orderline, to properly generate a project-based invoice from registered hours.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account + PUT /ledger/account/357150517 — bank account setup is likely not needed for this task and adds 2 calls.
POST /project/hourlyRates (409 error) — could be avoided by checking existing rates first with GET /project/hourlyRates.
POST /order/orderline with manual line — unnecessary if using project-based invoice generation directly.
